title: fastpath-ci-gate-dep-curation-scripts
author: Priya Nanduri
release_notes:
- Add staged fast-path CI gate to speed feedback on small PRs
- Introduce dep-curation scripts and dependency-snapshot.yaml used by CI
- Adjust test scheduler to prefer lightweight lanes and reduce flakiness
description:
Motivation: Our main CI pipeline provides strong coverage but slow feedback for small, iterative changes (median turnaround ~22m). This PR introduces a conservative 'fast-path' CI gate and companion dep-curation tooling to: (1) give developers quicker red/green on trivial edits, (2) keep heavy integration suites gated behind a staged smoke run, and (3) improve dependency hygiene with an automated curation snapshot.

Summary of changes: added a lightweight GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/ci-fastpath.yml) that runs lint, unit tests, and quick static checks in <10m for small diffs; modified ci/test-scheduler.go to classify PRs by changed paths and size; added scripts/dep_curate.py which generates dependency-snapshot.yaml (used by the pipeline to pin transitive ranges and skip noisy upgrades); adjusted existing lint/test workflows to accept the new fast-path gate as a pre-check; updated docs at docs/ci/fastpath.md describing gate behavior and escalation path.

Checklist: 
- [x] Fast-path workflow definition and runner labeling
- [x] Scheduler heuristics for path-based fast-path eligibility (docs updated)
- [x] Dep-curation script and sample snapshot committed
- [x] Integration tests for scheduler (unit-level)
- [x] Rollout plan included (gradual enablement via feature flag)

Rollout plan:
1) Stage: run fast-path on all PRs in opt-in mode (no gating) for 48h to collect metrics (latency, false negatives).
2) Gate: after metric validation, enable fast-path as a required check for small PRs (<10 changed files, only docs/ or pkg/ changes) with automatic fallback to full CI on mismatch.
3) Expand: incrementally relax size constraints and refine heuristics based on observed false-negative rate.

Risk & mitigations:
- Risk: fast-path might miss failures that only surface in integration tests. Mitigation: staged smoke gate (full CI runs in parallel until we reach confidence thresholds) and automatic fallback configured in the scheduler.
- Risk: dependency-snapshot might become stale. Mitigation: add weekly job (not in this PR) to propose curated updates and alert on drift; snapshot will be validated by the heavy CI lane.

Operational notes: 
- dep_curate.py accepts a lockfile and a policy file; it emits dependency-snapshot.yaml with pinned transitive versions and a lightweight justification field. The CI step will abort and post a comment if the snapshot validation fails (prevents accidental uncurated upgrades landing in main).
- The test scheduler exposes a small HTTP endpoint for metrics and a feature flag toggle (default off) so SRE can flip the gate during rollout.

Commands to exercise locally: 
- scripts/dep_curate.py --lockfile=pnpm-lock.yaml --policy=ci/dep-policy.yaml --out=ci/dependency-snapshot.yaml
- go test ./ci -run TestSchedulerFastPath -v
- act -j fastpath (developer convenience, requires act config)

Related work: ENG-4219 (fast-feedback CI workstream), ENG-4228 (dependency hygiene initiative), SUP-1024 (customer incident that motivated faster triage).

Commit summary (high level):
- Add fast-path CI workflow and small-run runner config
- Implement path/size heuristics in test scheduler and expose feature flag
- Add dep_curate.py, policy schema, and sample dependency-snapshot.yaml
- Adjust lint and release workflows to respect the fast-path gate and snapshot validation
- Update CI docs and rollout notes

Merge notes: squash-merged to main after CI green and approvals. Post-merge tasks: enable opt-in mode for 48h, monitor metrics dashboard (ci/fastpath -> latency, fallback-rate).
